content.title: About
content.content: Chipotle yogurt dip is a spicy condiment made from natural yogurt, chipotle paste, lime juice, and seasonings. It combines the creamy texture of yogurt with the smoky flavor of chipotle, delivering a light heat and fresh tang to dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chipotle is a smoked, dried jalapeño pepper that gives the dip its distinctive smoky taste.
The yogurt base makes the dip lighter and richer in probiotics compared with traditional mayo‑based dips.
It is commonly served with nachos, tacos, vegetable sticks, and seafood in Mexican cuisine.
The combination of lime and chipotle balances acidity and spiciness, aiding digestion.
Low in fat, this dip fits well into diet‑friendly menus.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: Yogurt provides live cultures that support a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low Fat Content
items.content: Compared with mayo‑based sauces, this dip contains fewer calories and saturated fats.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Lime adds vitamin C, which boosts immunity and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Capsaicin
items.content: Chipotle contains capsaicin, which may boost metabolism and has anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Calcium and Protein
items.content: Yogurt supplies calcium and plant‑based protein, beneficial for bones and muscles.

items.title: Lactose Intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort from the yogurt.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: The dip can be too hot for children or individuals with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Dairy Allergy
items.content: Those allergic to dairy should avoid this product.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: Some versions contain added salt; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve with nachos, tortillas, vegetable sticks, seafood, chicken wings, or use as a salad dressing. It also works well in sandwiches and burgers for an extra kick.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 1 °C–4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, consume within 5–7 days. Discard if it develops off‑odors or discoloration.

egg-sandwich-on-wheat-bread-with-meat.title: Egg and Meat Sandwich on Wheat Bread

content.title: About
content.content: An egg and meat sandwich on wheat bread is a nutritious snack consisting of whole‑grain bread, a boiled egg, tender cooked meat (such as chicken breast or ham), and optionally a slice of lettuce and a light sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wheat bread provides slow‑release energy thanks to its complex carbohydrates.
Eggs are one of the most affordable sources of complete protein, containing all essential amino acids.
Meat adds iron and vitamin B12, important for blood formation and nervous system function.
The protein‑carbohydrate combo makes this sandwich a popular post‑workout option.
Traditionally such sandwiches are served in school cafeterias and at sports events.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs and meat together provide a substantial amount of complete protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and egg supply vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat, especially beef, is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of complex carbs from wheat bread and protein helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Using whole‑grain bread adds fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed meats or sauces can raise the salt level, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked meat or eggs may harbor salmonella; ensure they are fully cooked.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat bread contains gluten, which is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, preferably cut in half. It can be served warm or cold, with added lettuce, tomato, or mustard according to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, separate the ingredients: store bread separately and keep meat and egg chilled.

infant-formula-similac-advance-powder-ma.title: Similac Advance Infant Formula, Powder, Made with Bottled Water

content.title: About
content.content: Similac Advance is a ready‑to‑feed infant formula powder designed for babies from birth to 12 months. It provides an optimal balance of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins and minerals, plus added DHA and lutein to support brain and eye development. The formula is prepared with bottled water, ensuring a consistent and safe composition.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Similac is one of the most recognized infant nutrition brands, with over 100 years on the market.
The protein blend includes partially hydrolyzed whey for better digestibility.
The formula is enriched with prebiotics to support a healthy gut microbiome.
Each package includes instructions for preparation with bottled water, reducing contamination risk.
Similac Advance has undergone clinical testing to confirm its safety and efficacy.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: A balanced mix of macro‑ and micronutrients supplies the energy, protein, and minerals needed for a growing infant.

items.title: Brain development
items.content: Added DHA and lutein aid neural development and visual function.

items.title: Gut health
items.content: Prebiotics promote beneficial bacteria, improving digestion and immunity.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, D and zinc help maintain the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Easy preparation
items.content: The powder dissolves quickly in bottled water, providing hygienic and precise nutrition.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some infants may be allergic to cow’s milk proteins; discontinue use at the first sign of reaction.

items.title: Incorrect reconstitution
items.content: Too concentrated or too diluted mixtures can lead to dehydration or excess calorie intake.

items.title: Storage
items.content: After opening, keep the container tightly sealed in a dry, cool place to prevent moisture ingress.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: Use the product before the printed expiration date, as nutrient quality may decline afterward.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Mix the specified amount of powder with 30 ml of bottled water (temperature 37 °C). Stir until fully dissolved and feed immediately. Do not use boiling water and do not leave the prepared formula at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened container in a dry, cool place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, use within 30 days and ensure no moisture enters the powder.

content.title: About
content.content: Lean beef refers to cuts of beef that are lower in fat, such as sirloin, round, tenderloin, flank steak, and lean ground beef. It is a widely eaten red meat valued for its savory flavor and rich supply of protein and minerals. Lean cuts are cooked by grilling, roasting, pan-searing, stewing, or slow cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lean beef cuts typically come from muscles that work harder, such as the round and sirloin, and contain less marbling.
Fat adds juiciness, so lean cuts can become dry if overcooked.
Ground beef is usually labeled with its lean-to-fat ratio, such as 90/10.
Marinating or slow cooking helps keep lean cuts tender.
Beef is among the most widely eaten meats in the world.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Beef provides complete protein, supporting muscle maintenance and repair.

items.title: Rich in heme iron
items.content: Beef contains heme iron, which the body absorbs more readily than iron from plants.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Rich in vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains B vitamins and selenium
items.content: Beef provides niacin, vitamin B6, and selenium.

items.title: Red meat consumption
items.content: Health organizations generally suggest limiting red meat, especially processed meat, because high intakes are linked to some health risks.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked beef, especially ground beef, can carry harmful bacteria. Cook ground beef to about 71 °C (160 °F) and steaks and roasts to at least about 63 °C (145 °F), then let them rest.

items.title: High-heat cooking
items.content: Charring or cooking meat at very high temperatures can form compounds that are best limited.

items.title: Iron and purines
items.content: People with iron overload conditions or gout should ask a healthcare professional about the amount of beef that is suitable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lean beef can be grilled, roasted, pan-seared, stir-fried, or slowly cooked in stews and braises. Slice steaks against the grain and avoid overcooking. Serve beef with vegetables and whole grains for a balanced meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw beef in the coldest part of the refrigerator, steaks and roasts for three to five days and ground beef for one to two days. Freeze for longer storage and thaw in the refrigerator. Store raw beef away from other foods and cooked beef in an airtight container for three to four days.

content.title: About
content.content: Multigrain Sun Chips are crunchy corn chips made from a blend of whole grains (wheat, corn, oats, rice) and lightly salted. They have a distinctive whole‑grain aroma and a mildly salty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sun Chips were introduced in 1991 as the first multigrain snack chips in the United States.
The recipe uses whole grains rather than just corn starch, giving them a more nutritious profile than regular corn chips.
The product contains no artificial colors or flavors.
Various regional flavors exist, such as BBQ, Sour Cream & Onion, and Cheddar & Sour Cream.
Packaging is made from recyclable material, and Frito‑Lay works on reducing the product’s carbon footprint.

items.title: Higher whole‑grain content
items.content: Provides whole grains that are sources of dietary fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: Unlike some other snacks, Sun Chips are cooked without partially hydrogenated oils, reducing trans‑fat levels.

items.title: Fiber source
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Whole grains contain phenolic compounds with antioxidant activity.

items.title: Reduced sodium compared to regular chips
items.content: Salt content is generally lower than that of traditional potato chips.

items.title: Grain allergies
items.content: May contain traces of wheat, barley, or oats, which is important for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although moderate, individuals monitoring sodium intake should account for it.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Like most dry snacks, they are calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy multigrain chips as a standalone snack, crumble them over salads for crunch, use as a base for nachos, or dip them in guacamole, yogurt‑based sauces, or cheese dips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the original sealed bag or an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For extended freshness, store in the refrigerator to maintain crispness and prevent staleness.

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken quesadilla is a Mexican dish consisting of a thin wheat or corn tortilla filled with shredded chicken, melted cheese, and sometimes vegetables, then toasted until golden. The result is a tender bite of seasoned chicken, stretchy cheese, and a lightly crisp exterior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “quesadilla” comes from the Spanish “queso,” meaning “cheese.”
Traditional Mexican quesadillas are made with corn tortillas, while U.S. versions often use flour tortillas.
Chicken is usually grilled or cooked in a chili‑based sauce, giving the filling a distinctive flavor.
Quesadillas are commonly served with salsa, guacamole, and sour cream.
The dish gained fast‑food popularity because it is quick to assemble and easy to eat on the go.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both chicken and cheese supply B6 and B12 vitamins, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Low in simple carbs
items.content: When made with whole‑grain tortillas, the dish has fewer simple carbohydrates, helping blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Micronutrients
items.content: Iron, zinc, and magnesium are present, contributing to immune support and energy production.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces and cheese often contain a lot of salt; those with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of cheese and oil makes quesadillas calorie‑rich, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Food‑borne bacteria
items.content: Chicken must be cooked thoroughly to prevent salmonella risk.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut the quesadilla into wedges and serve hot. It can be enjoyed alone or with salsa, guacamole, sour cream, and fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in a skillet or oven to restore crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: Stew, NFS (1504) is a ready‑to‑cook dry mix for making a hearty stew at home. The package contains dried vegetables, spices and a sauce base that, when rehydrated with water and briefly heated, turn into a flavorful dish suitable as a main course or side.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: NFS (Not From Scratch) indicates products that require no prior ingredient preparation.
The blend was developed by nutritionists to provide a balanced ratio of protein, carbs and fats.
Only natural spices are used, with no artificial flavorings.
Each serving is designed for 2–3 people and provides roughly 350 kcal.
Packaging is made from recyclable material to reduce environmental impact.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The dry mix includes legumes and meat proteins that help maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Dried vegetables and legumes supply fiber beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Natural sweeteners are used, making the dish suitable for those monitoring sugar intake.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The product provides B‑vitamins, iron and magnesium to support energy metabolism.

items.title: Moderate sodium content
items.content: Salt is added in modest amounts, helping to control overall sodium consumption.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: The mix contains peas and beans, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium excess if extra salt is added
items.content: It is recommended not to add additional salt during cooking to avoid high sodium levels.

items.title: Requires proper heating
items.content: Insufficient cooking temperature may leave harmful microorganisms alive.

items.title: Contains gluten
items.content: A small amount of gluten may be present from soy sauce used in the blend.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Transfer the contents of the packet into a pot, add 400 ml of water, bring to a boil and simmer for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally. Optional: add fresh vegetables or meat. Let stand for 2–3 minutes before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened packet in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer remaining dry mix to an airtight container and use within 3 months.
